criterion: A row is beta_blocking when a first-time beta user following docs-local/manual-en.html on the normal path would hit it; unusual operator flows and 1.0-grade completeness checks are ga_only.
gap_map_status_dimension_note: The gap-map classification records implementation or fixture readiness, while tier records release scope; this split does not dispute any gap-map status.

rows.reason: A first-time worker must connect a valid door before the seat can join and receive work, so failure here stops the documented normal path.
rows.required_change: Create the valid-worker-door fixture and capture the existing browser-door-connect-worker recipe; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: A first-time reviewer must connect an independent reviewer door before the documented submit-to-review lifecycle can close.
rows.required_change: Create the valid-reviewer-door fixture and capture the existing browser-door-connect-reviewer recipe; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: Prepare Team is the second onboarding step, so a first-time user needs an unambiguous selected-group state before proceeding.
rows.required_change: Run the browser-team-setup recipe against a disposable group; no further candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: The normal first-time path needs a worker and an independent reviewer, not an exact eight-seat 5-to-3 roster.
rows.known_limitation: The exact eight-seat topology still requires an independently arranged disposable runtime fixture.

rows.reason: The documented lifecycle requires an offered ticket to become claimed by a real identity, so a read-only claim surface blocks the normal path.
rows.required_change: Run the browser-ticket-offer-claim-live recipe against a live disposable offer; no further candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: An offer can expire while a first-time user follows the walkthrough, and accepting it or hiding the expiry would make the documented claim step silently wrong.
rows.required_change: Run the browser-ticket-offer-claim-expired recipe against an expired disposable offer; no further candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: A first-time user must see one submitted ticket close only after independent review, with no approval still pending.
rows.required_change: Run the browser-ticket-submit-independent-review recipe after an independent disposable review; no further candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: The normal path ends with the dashboard showing the real closed result, reviewer attribution, status transition, and a fresh cursor rather than stale state.
rows.required_change: Run the browser-result-visible recipe after the disposable ticket closes; no further candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: amended 2026-09-15 to product semantics: verify pause and cooperative stop on a disposable running seat and prove the unsupported Resume control is absent.
rows.known_limitation: AionUI intentionally has no Team resume operation; strict evidence must not invent one.

rows.reason: Credential rotation and recovery from an expired door occur after initial setup and are not part of the first-time normal path.
rows.known_limitation: Recovery from an expired or invalid door has not been validated for this beta.

rows.reason: Post-rotation cleanup counters matter to operators diagnosing an unusual recovery, not to a first-time user completing one clean connection.
rows.known_limitation: The recovery path still requires an independently arranged disposable rotated-door fixture.

rows.reason: A correctly provisioned first-time principal does not enter the permission-denied recovery path.
rows.known_limitation: The Personal dashboard may show a generic connection failure instead of the exact text “Permission denied.”

rows.reason: The normal path works with the host-selected theme and does not require a dashboard-specific light-to-dark switch.
rows.known_limitation: The Personal dashboard follows the host theme and does not provide its own light/dark theme switch.

rows.reason: The connection and saved-state indicators must both show Connected for a first-time user to know the seat actually joined.
rows.required_change: Run the existing browser-extension-join-state-joined recipe and retain the resulting evidence; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: Showing status for the wrong board would make the first-time joined state silently incorrect even though the page appears connected.
rows.required_change: Prepare the exact sandbox-home-acceptance board fixture and capture the existing status-loaded recipe; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: Automatic reconnect can occur during normal first use, and duplicate connections or hidden registration errors can make the first ticket flow silently wrong.
rows.required_change: Run the browser-extension-idempotent-reconnect recipe against a connected disposable seat; no further candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: The join form and one protected door input are the entry point for every first-time seat connection.
rows.required_change: Run the existing browser-extension-join-form recipe and retain the resulting evidence; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: A first-time connection must show useful status without retaining the secret door value, because a visible secret would be silently unsafe.
rows.required_change: Run the existing browser-extension-redacted-status-card recipe and retain the resulting evidence; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: amended 2026-09-15 to product semantics: verify the visible Open Quickstart hash link targets the already-visible #helper section.
rows.known_limitation: AionUI intentionally has no separate hidden settings panel; strict evidence must use the real visible navigation semantics.

rows.reason: A total Central outage is a failure drill outside the correctly configured first-time normal path.
rows.known_limitation: The Fleet Dashboard’s offline-only state has not been validated against a fixture where every configured Central is unavailable.

rows.reason: The dashboard must distinguish the active ticket created and claimed in the normal path from closed rows and an empty sentinel.
rows.required_change: Add a semantic ticket-status attribute or active-row marker in tools/fleet-dashboard/fleet_dashboard.py and read it in trusted_browser_state_v1/browser_observer.py.

rows.reason: A first-time operator needs at least one real board card to confirm the dashboard is connected to the configured project.
rows.required_change: Run the existing browser-fleet-board-cards recipe and retain the resulting evidence; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: Mixed healthy and unavailable Centrals require a multi-Central fault fixture that the first-time single-Central path does not use.
rows.known_limitation: Mixed healthy and unavailable Central isolation has not been validated for this beta.

rows.reason: The normal path uses the current Config-to-seats route, so only an operator seeking the legacy coordinator form would notice its absence.
rows.known_limitation: The legacy coordinator configuration form is not reachable; configure seats from the Fleet Dashboard Config route.

rows.reason: The normal dashboard path must open on Overview and show health for the connected fleet rather than an empty or wrong view.
rows.required_change: Run the existing browser-fleet-hub-overview recipe and retain the resulting evidence; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: Release-package manifest inspection is an operator release task, not the first-time ticket lifecycle.
rows.known_limitation: The Fleet release view’s manifest and package rows are outside the beta user-acceptance scope.

rows.reason: Reading the latest release tag is an operator release check and is not needed to join a seat or complete a ticket.
rows.known_limitation: The Fleet release view’s latest-tag display is outside the beta user-acceptance scope.

rows.reason: The dashboard must show real ticket counts as the first ticket moves through open, claimed, submitted, and closed states.
rows.required_change: Run the existing browser-fleet-ticket-counts recipe and retain the resulting evidence; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: A first-time operator needs an Updated state to distinguish current dashboard data from stale or invented status.
rows.required_change: Run the existing browser-fleet-updated-state recipe and retain the resulting evidence; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: A new board is normally empty before the first ticket is created, so the dashboard must represent zero tickets truthfully.
rows.required_change: Prepare an empty-board snapshot and execute the existing personal-board-snapshot-empty recipe; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: An empty link graph is optional context inspection and does not affect the first join, ticket, review, or dashboard flow.
rows.known_limitation: The Personal dashboard’s empty link-graph state has not been validated for this beta.

rows.reason: Pinned-memory highlights are reusable context features, not a prerequisite for the first ticket lifecycle.
rows.known_limitation: The Personal dashboard’s no-pinned-memory state has not been validated for this beta.

rows.reason: Looking up a nonexistent ticket is an error-recovery flow rather than the documented normal path using a real dispatched ticket.
rows.known_limitation: A missing ticket may produce a generic Personal dashboard failure instead of the exact text “ticket not found.”

rows.reason: A receipt-level surface identifier is 1.0-grade evidence completeness and has no first-time user-visible consequence.
rows.known_limitation: The Personal surface identifier is not part of the beta’s user-visible acceptance claims.

rows.reason: The Personal dashboard must identify the actual board or a first-time user can inspect and act on the wrong project without noticing.
rows.required_change: Prepare the exact sandbox-home-acceptance board fixture and capture the existing board-identity recipe; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: The normal Fleet view must show the configured project so a first-time operator can confirm registry routing before work starts.
rows.required_change: Prepare a fleet snapshot containing at least one project and capture the existing fleet-projects recipe; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: The docs do not prescribe keyboard input, but a keyboard-only first-time user follows the same normal tab flow and must be able to reveal Work with ArrowRight.
rows.required_change: Run the existing browser-personal-keyboard-tabs recipe and retain the resulting evidence; no candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: Searching an existing corpus is optional navigation after data exists and is not required to complete the first dispatched ticket.
rows.known_limitation: Personal dashboard search results require a preloaded matching corpus and are not validated for the beta normal path.

rows.reason: The normal user needs truthful claimed status, while inspecting the underlying lease expiry is an operator diagnostic.
rows.known_limitation: Personal dashboard lease-detail rendering has not been validated for this beta.

rows.reason: Quickstart is the first-time route into connecting the Home helper, so an absent action or raw internal JSON leaves the normal path incomplete or misleading.
rows.required_change: Run the browser-final-quickstart-candidate-flow recipe on the clean candidate runtime; no further candidate change is indicated.

rows.reason: Creating and healing a deterministic Central 503 is a fault-injection exercise outside the healthy first-time normal path.
rows.known_limitation: Automated Fleet recovery from a controlled Central 503 has not been validated for this beta.

rows.reason: A guarded release operation and rollback is an operator-only release flow, not a first-time seat or ticket action.
rows.known_limitation: The Fleet Dashboard does not yet expose canonical rollback-result and success-effect fields for guarded release operations.
